name: Arlington
seo_title: 5 Christmas Events for Kids in Arlington, WA 2026
seo_desc: 5 Christmas events for kids in Arlington, WA, 3 free: Hometown Holidays Kickoff and Tree Lighting at Legion Park and more.
lede: Arlington calls its season Hometown Holidays: a tree lighting on Olympic Avenue at the end of November, then a Santa Parade, free carousel and Ferris wheel rides and Breakfast with Santa in early December.
celebrates: Arlington's Hometown Holidays starts on the last Saturday of November, when Olympic Avenue closes to traffic and the Christmas tree in Legion Park is lit at 5 pm, with fire pits, s'mores, carolers, falling snow and Mrs. Claus at the gazebo. The first Saturday of December brings the Santa Parade on Olympic Avenue, Santa visits at the Legion Park gazebo, wagon rides from City Hall and holiday movies at the Olympic Theater. A free holiday carousel and Ferris wheel run next to Legion Park for ten days, and the Arlington Education Foundation serves Breakfast with Santa. A local church shows hundreds of nativities, and the Stilly Valley Chamber runs a Charm Walk.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Arlington held its Santa Parade day on Saturday, December 6. The city listed the Santa Breakfast, the Charm Walk, a Holiday Farmers Market from 10 am to 2 pm, the Santa Parade at noon on Olympic Avenue, a festive sweater contest at 12:30 pm in Legion Park, Santa visits from 12:30 to 3 pm, wagon rides until 4 pm, the Holiday Carousel and Ferris Wheel from noon to 7 pm, movies at the Olympic Theater at 2 pm and a high school winter bazaar.
facts: Arlington started as two rival towns. In 1890 Haller City was platted at the forks of the Stillaguamish River, and Arlington, named after Lord Henry Arlington, a cabinet member of King Charles II of England, was platted half a mile away. Business slowly moved up the hill to Arlington, and in 1903 the two were incorporated as one town. Division Street is the reminder that there were once two. Arlington even sent a 200 foot tree to the World's Fair in Chicago, where it stood as the tallest flagstaff.
trains: The railroad decided Arlington's future. When the Seattle, Lake Shore and Eastern arrived in 1890, the depot went to Arlington on higher ground instead of riverside Haller City, the first freight train came on July 23, and the first streets were named for the railroad's construction men. The Northern Pacific later ran a 28 mile line to Darrington. Today the Depot Visitor Center sits at Legion Park, and the closest passenger trains are Amtrak Cascades at Stanwood and Everett Station. For a holiday train ride, the Northwest Railway Museum runs its North Pole Limited Santa Train from North Bend.

On the first Saturday of December, Santa and Mrs. Claus ride a wagon down Olympic Avenue at noon, followed by Santa visits at the Legion Park gazebo.
The city sets up free rides next to Legion Park for about ten days in December, with a sensory friendly hour on Sundays.

kidfact: Arlington once sent a tree that was 200 feet tall all the way to the World's Fair in Chicago, where it became the tallest flagpole at the fair.
faq: When is the Arlington tree lighting?

The City of Arlington lights its Christmas tree in Legion Park at 5 pm during the Hometown Holidays kickoff on the last Saturday of November. Olympic Avenue closes to traffic from 4 to 7 pm for strolling, shopping, carolers, fire pits and falling snow, and Mrs. Claus visits the gazebo. Free parking and shuttles run from two nearby schools.
When is the Arlington Santa Parade?

The Hometown Holidays Santa Parade rolls down Olympic Avenue at noon on the first Saturday of December. The city says it features a wagon carrying Santa and Mrs. Claus, classic cars, dancers, scouts and community floats. Afterward Santa visits the Legion Park gazebo until 3 pm and wagon rides leave from City Hall.
Is the Arlington holiday carousel free?

Yes. The City of Arlington says the Holiday Carousel and Ferris Wheel next to Legion Park are provided at no cost, funded by the Arlington Hotel/Motel Tax grant. The rides run for about ten days in early December, from noon to 7 pm most days and noon to 6 pm on Sundays, with a sensory friendly hour on Sunday mornings.
Where is the closest train station to Arlington, WA?

Arlington has no passenger trains today. The closest stops are the Amtrak Cascades station in Stanwood and Everett Station, which also has the Sounder N Line on weekdays and the Empire Builder. Arlington's Depot Visitor Center at Legion Park recalls the railroad depot that helped the town win its early rivalry with Haller City.
intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in Arlington for 2026, and here is what he found: 5 family events, 3 of them free. The magic runs from November 28 (Hometown Holidays Kickoff and Tree Lighting at Legion Park) through December 13, with Hometown Holidays Kickoff and Tree Lighting at Legion Park (November 28), Holiday Carousel and Ferris Wheel at Legion Park (from December 4) and Breakfast with Santa at Presidents Elementary (December 5) along the way. We check every date on the host’s own website or an official city calendar, and each listing links straight there. For the rest of the state, see our Washington Christmas events for kids guide.
